module purpose: neorv32_hwspinlock holds 32 one-bit locks in lock_q: a bus access with addr(7) = '0' sets the lock whose index matches addr(6 downto 2) on a read and clears it on a write, while the registered response returns that lock's previous bit, and a read with addr(7) = '1' returns all 32 lock bits (lines 36-51, 58-74).

use-case flows.value: per-lock bit: set to '1' by a read access (not rw) and cleared to '0' by a write access to the lock selected by addr(6 downto 2), when stb = '1' and addr(7) = '0'
test-and-set result: the selected lock's bit as it was before the same clock edge's update (lock_q and sel) for addr(7) = '0', or all 32 lock bits for addr(7) = '1', on a read access
bus acknowledge copied from the strobe and an error bit tied to '0' on every clock edge
all lock bits cleared to '0' and the bus response forced to rsp_terminate_c while rstn_i = '0'

conceptual assets.concept: Spinlock state -- whether each of the 32 locks is currently held or free
conceptual assets.reasoning: The lock flow updates each bit only under `if (bus_req_i.stb = '1') and (bus_req_i.addr(7) = '0') and (sel(i) = '1') then lock_q(i) <= not bus_req_i.rw;` (lines 44-45), so a read acquires (sets) and a write releases (clears) the addressed lock. The read-out flow returns `bus_rsp_o.data <= lock_q and sel;` (line 68) in the same clocked process edge (line 62) as the update edge (line 43), so the requester receives the selected lock's value before its own access set it: the test-and-set relation between returned bit and new state depends on lock_q holding exactly the value written by the last acquire, release or reset. Integrity is Established from lines 42, 45 and 68. Availability is also Established: lock_q is assigned only under the line 44 condition or the reset arm (line 42), so a held lock is preserved between accesses until a write to its index or reset, and its value is delivered on every qualifying read (lines 68, 70). Confidentiality is not established: line 70 returns all lock bits on any read with addr(7) = '1', and no line restricts the requester (bus_req_i.priv and bus_req_i.src have no local use). lock_q stores the state (occurrence 3, CLOCKED_BY clk_i, line 45) and its records show its use toward an output field (CARRIES bus_rsp_o.data at occurrence 5, line 70; SOURCES bus_rsp_o.data at occurrence 4, line 68). bus_req_i and bus_rsp_o are records carrying complete bus transactions (address, write data, byte enables, strobe, read/write, acknowledge, read data), so the transport rule excludes them and their fields: bus_req_i.rw is not listed as a setting point and bus_rsp_o is not listed as an exit; this is a mapping limitation, not absence of the flow. clk_i and rstn_i are clock and reset inputs (SEQUENCES line 43, RESETS line 41).

conceptual assets.concept: Lock-index selection decision -- which of the 32 locks a bus access acquires, releases or tests
conceptual assets.reasoning: The decision is computed per lock by `sel(i) <= '1' when (bus_req_i.addr(6 downto 2) = std_ulogic_vector(to_unsigned(i, 5))) else '0';` (line 51), a comparison result (GATED_BY bus_req_i.addr at occurrence 3). The lock flow depends on it: it is a term of the update condition of lock_q(i) (line 44; GATES lock_q at occurrence 2), so only the lock whose index matches is set or cleared. The read-out flow depends on it: it masks the test-and-set response `bus_rsp_o.data <= lock_q and sel;` (line 68; SOURCES bus_rsp_o.data at occurrence 4), so only the addressed lock's prior bit is returned. Integrity is Established: a wrong selection would acquire or release a lock other than the addressed one and report another lock's prior state, breaking the per-lock test-and-set relation of lines 44-45 and 68. sel is combinational (storage none), so no storage availability claim is made; confidentiality is not established. The map lists sel as not reached from any source because its value arms are the constants '1' and '0' (line 51); its own value is still the decision. The address field it compares, bus_req_i.addr, belongs to a transport record and is not listed.
